input_equivalence.live: one app, one process-wide run lease, and exactly one active arm per physical run; Basalt and XRSLAM share the frozen 640x480 raw sensor contract while ARKit owns its private production-equivalent sensor chain; trajectories are not identical
input_equivalence.replay: Basalt and XRSLAM in the same app consume the exact same content-addressed EuRoC cam0+IMU manifest; ARKit replay is forbidden
input_equivalence.winner_selection: Basalt/XRSLAM accuracy uses replay; live soak compares feasibility, latency proxies, memory, thermal, battery proxy, transport loss, and tracking health; ARKit is a system reference arm and never ground truth

xrslam.artifact_platform_limit: object build versions are mixed; the highest observed iOS minimum is 26.2 despite the receipt declaring 14.0. The test device runs iOS 26.6. Both values are receipted; neither substitutes for the other.

arkit_reference.configuration: ARWorldTrackingConfiguration; autofocus=true; worldAlignment=gravity; lightEstimation=false; planeDetection=horizontal; locked 1920x1440 high-resolution-capable format; main delegate queue; resetTracking+removeExistingAnchors
arkit_reference.accuracy_role: live system reference only; no external ground truth and no EuRoC replay

unified_bench.lease_handoff: selected native handle must be destroyed and process-global engine ownership cleared before another arm may acquire the lease
unified_bench.framework_symbol_policy: only the selected C bridge API is exported; OpenCV symbols are private to each two-level dylib

apps.backend_policy: cpu for Basalt/XRSLAM; apple_arkit for ARKit reference
apps.uses_arkit_semantics: true only when an ARSession is constructed for the selected arm; framework linkage alone is not sensor use

live_soak.camera_target_hz: 30 for Basalt/XRSLAM; selected production ARVideoFormat FPS for ARKit
live_soak.camera_format: all three arms score at 1920x1440; ARKit via its production ARVideoFormat, Basalt/XRSLAM by replaying the luma plane of that same ARFrame.capturedImage stream
live_soak.camera_session_preset: ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.videoFormat locked 1920x1440 for the recording/ARKit arm; candidate arms consume the recording and open no capture session
live_soak.xrslam_official_pixel_preprocess_deviati: official iOS sample requests 32BGRA then OpenCV BGRA2GRAY; the shared Basalt/XRSLAM live contract deliberately uses the same full-range NV12 luma plane for both candidates and records this deviation

validity.loss_scope: cumulative from live sensor start across the full measurement and final drain; any loss makes the run invalid

live_soak.metric_scope: the live clock, CPU accounting, and system sampling start before selected estimator/session initialization; the complete 300-second product session is scored with no excluded warm-up, and cumulative validity also covers final drain

feasibility_gates.processed_fps_min: 27 for a 30 FPS arm; otherwise 90 percent of the frozen selected format FPS

replacement_policy.candidate_absolute_gates: every live feasibility gate and every EuRoC accuracy gate must pass
replacement_policy.same_device_dominance: candidate first usable pose delivery, p95 pipeline latency, transport loss, thermal dwell, peak footprint, CPU and battery proxy must not be worse than the ARKit reference arm on the same device, OS and shared capture; accuracy must be strictly better
replacement_policy.live_accuracy_claim: blocked without external ground truth; ARKit live poses are a system reference, not ground truth
replacement_policy.production_replacement_status: blocked until absolute gates, same-device dominance, external-ground-truth live accuracy, and later PocketWorld product-shadow gates all pass
accuracy_evidence_required: on the shared device recording: loop-closure error, static-segment drift and coarse scale error each strictly lower than ARKit on the identical frames
on EuRoC: every absolute accuracy gate passed
replacement_policy.resource_bar_rationale: running cooler is not a product goal; not regressing is the requirement
replacement_policy.realtime_bar: 1920x1440 at 30 fps, p95 <= 66.7 ms, zero loss

diagnostic_resolution.derivation: deterministic downscale of the 1920x1440 recording; hash frozen alongside the master
diagnostic_resolution.purpose: failure triage only: when a candidate fails at 1920x1440, rerun at the upstream-native scale to separate 'the algorithm cannot carry 9x the pixels' from 'we ported its pixel-unit parameters wrong'

preview_contract.arkit_arm: the ARSession's own camera background; no second capture session
preview_contract.replay_arms: display the frame currently being replayed; no second camera session
preview_contract.ownership: UI displays only; the coordinator state machine remains the sole camera lifecycle owner
preview_contract.shows: the luma plane of frames the arm has already accepted, which for Basalt and XRSLAM is exactly the algorithm input. For ARKit it is a subset: ARKit also receives chroma. The preview is therefore faithful for the candidates and understates ARKit.

resource_measurement.arkit: measured live during the recording capture
resource_measurement.candidates: measured during replay-paced 300 s with the device stationary
resource_measurement.decomposition: candidate live cost = replay-paced compute cost + camera-capture cost, where the camera term is measured once by a null run (capture on, no VIO, 300 s) and is identical for both candidates
resource_measurement.recorder_overhead: the recording capture pays disk-write cost that the replays do not; it is instrumented inside the recorder and reported, not silently absorbed into ARKit's numbers
resource_measurement.rationale: thermal load comes from compute, not from the operator's arm; replay is repeatable

replay.trajectory_frame: body_imu_frame for Basalt, XRSLAM BODY_POSE, and EuRoC p_RS_R/q_RS; camera pose is forbidden for accuracy scoring

answers: throughput, latency and loss at production resolution
does_not_answer: absolute accuracy: this channel has no ground truth

answers: absolute ATE and RPE against real ground truth
whether our integration reproduces upstream behaviour
does_not_answer: anything about ARKit: ARKit cannot be fed EuRoC

revision_history.summary: three arms run separate live soaks; Basalt/XRSLAM at 640x480, ARKit at 1920x1440

scoring resolution unified at 1920x1440 for all three arms; one device recording sourced from ARFrame.capturedImage replaces per-arm live soaks as the shared trajectory input; 640x480 demoted to a non-scoring diagnostic; replacement bar raised from not-worse-than to strictly-better-than ARKit on accuracy; single monotonic clock domain pinned; live camera preview required
revision_history.rationale: Production already runs ARKit at 1920x1440 on this device, so 1920x1440 is the requirement, not a cost to be negotiated. Scoring a 640x480 candidate against a 1920x1440 ARKit would be a false comparison. Three separate handheld soaks can never share speed, angle, lighting or time, so they were never an A/B.

clock_domain.forbidden_rationale: On Darwin std::chrono::steady_clock is CLOCK_MONOTONIC == mach_continuous_time and includes device sleep; mach_absolute_time excludes it. Measured 2026-08-30, timebase 125/3: steady_clock 43147376131416 ns (11.985 h) vs mach_absolute_time 42087301077208 ns (11.691 h).
clock_domain.defect_of_record: 2026-08-29 device run: 97 s soak reported p95 81219463.2 ms and first pose 81219577 ms; the 113.8 ms difference was the real first-pose latency
clock_domain.invariant: any latency exceeding run elapsed plus 250 ms scheduling slack invalidates the run

device_recording.purpose: share one physical capture across every arm so speed, angle, lighting and time are not resampled per arm. Basalt and XRSLAM additionally receive byte-identical input, because both consume only the luma plane that is stored.
device_recording.source_rationale: iOS grants the rear camera to exactly one session, so ARSession and AVCaptureSession cannot coexist. Recording from ARKit's own frames routes around that: the ARKit arm runs live while the identical frames are persisted for the candidates.
device_recording.imu: CoreMotion recorded in parallel; independent of the camera session
device_recording.arkit_pose_role: same-input system reference; still not ground truth
device_recording.compression_policy: lossy encoding forbidden; the recording is algorithm input, not a preview
device_recording.reuse: frozen by SHA-256 and replayed for every future iteration at zero further capture cost
device_recording.known_gap: candidates are scored on ARKit-conditioned imagery: ARKit owns autofocus and exposure during the capture. A production replacement would drive its own AVCaptureSession. This must be cross-checked with one AVFoundation recording before any production shadow, and must never be described as already verified.
crude_metric_protocol: start and end on the same physical marker so loop-closure error bounds accumulated drift
hold stationary on a desk for 10 s at the start and at the end to measure static drift
include a known-length baseline in the scene for a coarse metric scale check
device_recording.chroma_asymmetry: ARKit consumes the full 420f biplanar buffer (luma and chroma) live during the capture; the recording stores the luma plane only, because that is the entire frozen input contract for Basalt and XRSLAM. So the three arms share one capture, not one byte stream. 'Byte-identical' is true between the two candidates and must never be claimed for ARKit.

upstream_scale_adaptation.problem: Basalt's official euroc_config.json is tuned for 752x480 and XRSLAM's iPhone config for 640x480. Patch size, pyramid depth, detection grid and feature caps are all in pixel units, so feeding 1920x1440 through an unchanged config measures our port, not the algorithm.
forbidden: any value without a recorded derivation
silently reusing an upstream default at a scale it was never defined for

calibration.intrinsics_rationale: intrinsics are a hardware property, not an ARKit algorithm output, and the recorded frames are exactly the frames those intrinsics describe, so no extrapolation is needed
calibration.intrinsics_cross_check: the frozen 640x480 upstream intrinsics scaled by 3 must agree; disagreement means the formats differ by more than a scale and must halt the run
calibration.extrinsics_rationale: a rigid IMU-to-camera transform is resolution independent
calibration.distortion_known_limitation: upstream supplies zero distortion coefficients. The same physical distortion acts over three times the pixel radius at 1920x1440, so this approximation is worse here than at 640x480. Declared, not hidden.
calibration.uses_arkit: intrinsics only; no ARKit pose, tracking state or algorithm output feeds a candidate arm
